# Usability Audit — settings flow

## Executive summary

Two findings on the settings flow, read from source. The worst is a loss of user control
that no Nielsen heuristic expresses: autosave owns the commit moment, so the person
becomes the responder rather than the initiator. It is filed against Shneiderman #7 and
carries its own `health` row, because the attribution follows the evidence rather than the
rubric (§4.1).

## Design health

39/44 · 73% · Good. Ten Nielsen heuristics plus the one Shneiderman principle a finding
was attributed to.

## Prioritized fixes

1. [P1] Autosave takes the commit moment away from the user
2. [P2] "Delete" and "Remove" name the same destructive action

## Findings

### [P1] Autosave takes the commit moment away from the user

- **Issue Description:** The settings form writes on every keystroke after a 400 ms idle.
  There is no Save control, no way to abandon an edit, and no indication of when a write
  happened. The person cannot choose the moment their change takes effect.
- **Framework Violation:** Shneiderman #7 — support internal locus of control (primary;
  corroborated by Nielsen #3 user control and freedom, which covers the missing exit but
  not the loss of initiative). This is what the Shneiderman lens uniquely expresses, so it
  is cited standalone and carries its own `health` item.
- **Priority:** P1 Major — fix before release; the user cannot predict or prevent a write
  to their own account settings.
- **Evidence:** potential — unverified; no running app was observed. `src/Settings.tsx:58`
  debounces straight into the mutation; there is no submit handler in the file.
- **Recommended Fix:** add an explicit Save, or keep autosave and add an undo window plus a
  written-at indicator.

### [P2] "Delete" and "Remove" name the same destructive action

- **Issue Description:** The row control reads "Remove" and its confirmation dialog reads
  "Delete permanently", so the user confirms a different verb than the one they chose.
- **Framework Violation:** Nielsen #4 — consistency and standards.
- **Priority:** P2 Minor — fix in the next pass; the action is correct, the naming is not.
- **Evidence:** potential — unverified; `src/Settings.tsx:112` and `src/Confirm.tsx:19`.
- **Recommended Fix:** use one verb for the action everywhere it is named.

## Appendix

- **Mode:** static. No running app was observed, so both findings are labelled
  `potential — unverified`.
- **Frameworks applied:** nielsen-10, shneiderman-8. The AI heuristics are not applicable
  (no AI features on this surface) and NPCIS was not applied.
- **Coverage / not inspected:** the billing and notification panels were in scope and were
  not inspected; no runtime behaviour was observed anywhere.
